D010-D005_h001.question:
It’s been a weird year. About seven months back I just sort of went flat inside. I’d drive the cab, pick people up, drop them off, and feel nothing. Things I used to enjoy on my days off – football on TV, going for a drink with mates – I just stopped caring. Even small stuff, like choosing what to eat or what shirt to wear, feels like this huge decision now. I just stare at the menu or my wardrobe and can’t make up my mind. My ex says I’m like a robot with our son, like I’m there but switched off.

Then, about two months ago, it flipped. I’ve been on edge, snapping at passengers over nothing, shouting if someone hesitates getting in the car. I can’t sit still at the taxi rank – I’m pacing, tapping the steering wheel, walking circles around the car. When I talk, it’s like my mouth runs ahead of my brain; people tell me to slow down because they can’t keep up.

I’ve also been spending money like crazy – new stereo, clothes, online stuff I don’t need – my account’s a mess and my ex is furious. Lately I keep feeling like radio songs or people’s comments are secretly about me, like there’s some message. And sometimes when I’m driving, I get this crawling, buzzing feeling on my skin, like insects moving under my shirt, but there’s nothing there when I check.
D010-D005_h001.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
D010-D005_h001.answer: D & C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features & Schizophrenia

D010-D005_h002.question:
I’m not really sure where to start. The last year’s been…strange.  

For about a couple of months over the summer, I felt like I was on overdrive. On set I was bouncing between three different shoots and rewriting scripts at 3 a.m., storyboarding whole seasons in one night, barely sleeping but not feeling tired. I’d talk so fast in meetings that producers would ask me to slow down, but my head was moving ahead of my mouth. My mood would flip in seconds—one minute I’d be on top of the world, convinced this was my “genius phase,” and the next I’d snap at my AD for the smallest thing. I drove way too fast between locations, did more coke than I’m proud of, hooked up recklessly. It felt like nothing could touch me…until it all kind of crashed.  

Since then—five months, maybe more—I’ve been mostly flat. Getting out of bed feels heavy. I stare at scripts and can’t push myself to start, my head feels full of fog.  

On top of that, I sometimes hear this voice, not mine, commenting on what I’m doing. And I keep feeling like this actress I worked with is secretly in love with me, sending me “messages” through her Instagram posts, even though I know that sounds off.
D010-D005_h002.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
D010-D005_h002.answer: D & C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features & Schizophrenia

D010-D005_h003.question:
It’s been a really strange year. Around seven months ago I started feeling…off. For the last five months or so I’ve mostly just felt hollow, like someone turned the volume down inside me. Things I used to enjoy—reading with my kids, planning creative therapy activities—feel pointless. I stare at the closet in the morning and can’t even decide what to wear; I’ll change outfits three or four times and still feel like I picked wrong. Even choosing what to eat can take forever.

But before that, for about two months, I was the opposite. I barely sat down. At work I was pacing between sessions, reorganizing my materials over and over. At home I was constantly starting projects—repainting a room at 2 a.m., driving way too fast at night just to “clear my head.” My husband kept telling me to slow down. I was talking nonstop in sessions, going off on tangents with parents and colleagues.

During that time—and sometimes since—I’ve been convinced a dad of one of my students has feelings for me. I catch myself thinking he’s sending me secret messages through small comments or looks. I’ve also occasionally seen people in the corner of my eye—like a figure standing in the hallway at school—but when I look properly, no one’s there.
D010-D005_h003.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
D010-D005_h003.answer: D & C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features & Schizophrenia

D010-D005_h004.question:
I’m not really sure how to put this all together, but something’s been very wrong this past year.

About six or seven months ago, I hit this…high. I was constantly on edge and snapping at everyone, even my kids and the teachers I work with, over the smallest things. At the same time I had this nonstop energy. I’d be up late redoing therapy materials, reorganizing the whole clinic, starting side projects for an online speech course, all at once. I talked so fast in sessions that parents would tell me to slow down, but I felt like if I stopped talking the ideas would disappear. I couldn’t sit still in meetings—pacing in the hallway, rubbing my hands, tapping my feet. I even wired a chunk of our savings into this private speech-tech startup I’d barely researched; it felt “meant to be” in the moment.

Around then I became convinced this well-known therapist I follow online has feelings for me—tiny posts or likes feel like secret messages. Sometimes I feel as if something is brushing along my arms or crawling on my skin, but there’s nothing there.

More recently it all crashed. For about five months now I’ve been crying at the smallest thing, can’t make myself prep sessions, and my mind feels thick, like I’m thinking through mud. I keep replaying what happened, but I can’t tell where one phase ended and the other started. I just know my work and home life have both really suffered.
D010-D005_h004.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
D010-D005_h004.answer: D & C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features & Schizophrenia

D010-D005_h005.question:
I guess this all really started about seven months ago. For a couple of months I felt like I was on overdrive. At the library I couldn’t sit still at the reference desk—I was darting between shelves, rearranging things that didn’t need it, starting new projects before I finished the old ones. I was calling old classmates, chatting up patrons, even going out after work, which is very unlike me. I’d talk and talk and it was hard to stop, even when people looked uncomfortable.

I also started ordering books and clothes online late at night, like it was urgent. The credit cards are a mess now; I’m embarrassed to even open the statements.

Around that time I became convinced that one of our regular patrons had feelings for me—little things he did felt like secret messages. It still kind of feels that way, even though I know it sounds odd. And sometimes I get this strange metallic taste in my mouth out of nowhere, like I’m tasting something that isn’t there.

For the past five months, though, everything’s gone flat. I don’t enjoy reading anymore, which is terrifying for a librarian. I feel hollow, like my feelings are behind glass. My thoughts feel thick and slow, like I’m moving through fog. I make mistakes at work, forget what I was doing mid-task, and after my shift I just go home and sit, not really doing anything. It’s getting hard to keep up.
D010-D005_h005.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
D010-D005_h005.answer: D & C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features & Schizophrenia

D010-D005_h006.question:
I’ve been out in the woods most days like always, but for the past couple of months I feel like I’m wound way too tight. It’s like I’ve got this motor running in me all the time. I’ll hike my patrol route, then instead of resting I start clearing brush, fixing fences, planning new projects for the station. I can’t sit still, and when I’m in the cabin I just pace and keep coming up with “great ideas.”

I catch myself snapping at people over nothing—other rangers, hikers, even on the radio. Little things set me off: someone walking off-trail, paperwork not done just right, and I’m suddenly barking at them.

I’ve also been talking a lot more. Once I start, I just go on and on—about new tourism programs, buying extra land, opening some kind of wilderness retreat. I already put money into a couple of online “eco-investments” without really checking them out, more than I can afford on my salary.

There’s this woman from the regional office—I’m sure she’s been sending me signals, like special meaning in her emails, like she cares for me. And when I’m alone at night, I hear voices sometimes, like people talking just outside the cabin or calling my name, but when I go out, there’s no one there.
D010-D005_h006.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
D010-D005_h006.answer: D & A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features & Schizophrenia

D010-D005_h007.question:
It’s been about two months now where I’ve felt like I’m running on some kind of internal battery that never runs out. I wake up after a few hours of sleep feeling wired, almost high on my own thoughts. My husband keeps telling me to sit down, but I just can’t—I’m pacing around the apartment, reorganizing things at 3 a.m., pitching three different story ideas to my editor in one email, talking so fast he has to tell me to slow down.

I feel…brilliant, invincible almost. I’ve been driving way too fast between interviews, weaving through traffic because it feels like I can react to everything before it happens. I’ve also started experimenting with stuff I normally wouldn’t touch—some pills a friend offered “just to stay sharp” on deadline. I didn’t really think about what could go wrong.

At the same time, I’ve become convinced people are watching me. When I’m out reporting, I notice the same car behind me for blocks, or I’m sure my emails are being tracked. I keep smelling this strange chemical, like burnt plastic or cleaning fluid, even when no one else notices it. I can’t tell if I’m just being paranoid or if something is actually happening, but it’s making it harder to focus on my work and my family.
D010-D005_h007.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D010-D005_h008.question:
It’s been about two months now where I just feel… revved up all the time. On trips, I can’t sit still in the jumpseat; I’m bouncing my leg, getting up to “recheck” things that don’t need checking. Even on layovers, I’m pacing hotel hallways at 3 a.m. instead of sleeping.

My mood is all over the place. One moment I’m on top of the world, convinced I’m about to do something huge with my life, like I’m meant for something way beyond just working flights. Then suddenly I’m snapping at coworkers over tiny things or getting irrationally angry when a passenger hesitates putting their bag away. The switches happen so fast it’s exhausting.

I also can’t seem to shut up. Once I start talking in the galley or with friends, it feels physically uncomfortable to stop, like I’ll explode if there’s silence. I talk over people without meaning to.

I’ve been spending money like crazy—designer luggage, first-class tickets on my days off, random online stuff I don’t need. My credit cards are maxed; my sister’s furious because I borrowed money and blew through it.

Sometimes I get this absolute conviction that I have a special purpose, like I’m being prepared for some important mission. And every now and then I’ll suddenly taste something metallic or bitter in my mouth out of nowhere, even when I’m not eating anything.
D010-D005_h008.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
D010-D005_h008.answer: D & A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features & Schizophrenia

D010-D005_h009.question:
It’s been about two months now where I’ve just felt… turned up way too high. On trips I’m buzzing, like I’ve had ten coffees even when I haven’t. I can’t sit still in the jumpseat; I’m always pacing the galley, talking to passengers, volunteering to take extra legs. I feel ridiculously good, almost invincible, like I’m on top of everything, even when I’m clearly not.

My crew say I talk so fast they can’t keep up, and I keep jumping from one topic to another. On layovers I’ve been going on these crazy shopping runs—designer bags, makeup, gadgets—maxed out two credit cards. I’m behind on rent now, but in the moment it feels like I *have* to buy it.

What’s really freaking me out is I’ve started thinking my ex was cheating on me with other crew, even though I’ve never actually caught him or seen proof. I’ll replay tiny things, like a look or a text, and convince myself it proves he was lying. And sometimes in hotel rooms or even on the plane, I’ll see a person standing in the aisle or in the corner of the room, but when I look again, no one’s there. I can’t tell if I’m just exhausted from flying or if something’s really wrong.

A. Schizophrenia
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D010-D005_h010.question:
It’s been going on maybe a couple of months now. My wife says I’ve been “too happy,” kind of wound up. I just feel like I’ve got all this energy all the time. I’m up before dawn, pacing around the building, checking every light, every lock, doing things that don’t really need doing. I can’t sit still long enough to watch TV or even finish a cup of coffee.

I talk a lot more than usual. Once I start, it’s like my mouth won’t shut off. At work the tenants try to walk away and I just keep going, jumping from one topic to another. Silence feels…uncomfortable, almost painful.

I’ve also been getting these ideas about money. I put a big chunk of our savings into this online “property venture” my neighbor told me about, without really understanding it. My wife was furious. I just felt so sure it would make us rich.

At the same time, I’m convinced something’s wrong inside me. I keep thinking my organs are rotting or changing shape, like my stomach is dissolving. And sometimes I see people in the hallways who aren’t really there—just standing at the end of the corridor, watching me—and when I look again, they’re gone.

    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D010-D005_h011.question:
It’s been about a month now where I feel like I’m either way up or snapping at people, and it can flip in the same hour. I’ll be working on a campaign, feeling amazing, like my ideas are genius and I’m on top of everything, and then suddenly I’m furious because someone is “too slow” replying to an email, or I start crying for no reason. I can’t sit still—I’m pacing during Zoom calls, cleaning my apartment at 2 a.m., starting new projects before I’ve finished the last ones. My mind just won’t shut up. It’s like a dozen tabs open and all blasting at once, and I lose track of what I was even thinking.

Work has really suffered—I miss deadlines, send rambling messages to clients, and then feel embarrassed later.

Another thing I’m almost afraid to say: I’m convinced this guy I collaborate with remotely has feelings for me, even though we barely talk outside work. I read into every emoji, every delay, like it’s a secret message. And sometimes, especially at night, I feel this crawling or light pressure on my skin, like someone’s brushing past me or touching my arm, but there’s no one there.

    C. Binge-Eating Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia

D010-D005_h012.question:
It’s been about a month now where I feel like I can’t settle. I’m up before dawn, pacing around the house, reorganizing cupboards, starting projects I never finish. My husband keeps telling me to sit down, but I feel almost driven, like if I stop moving something terrible will happen.

My mood has been all over the place. One minute I’m talking a mile a minute, feeling oddly excited, planning to repaint the whole house, and the next I snap at him for no good reason, or burst into tears. I can hear myself getting sharp or giddy, but I can’t seem to rein it in.

What’s really scaring me are my thoughts. They don’t slow down. It’s like a radio stuck between stations, everything at once, and I can’t find the “off” switch. Along with that, I’ve become convinced something awful is coming — like the world is on the brink of collapsing, that none of this will matter soon. It doesn’t feel like “a worry,” it feels like a fact. Sometimes I even smell this strong burning or rotting odor in the house, but no one else notices it, and there’s nothing there. All of this has made it very hard to manage normal things at home.
D010-D005_h012.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Bipolar II Disorder
    C. Binge-Eating Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia

D010-D005_h013.question:

At the gym I’m “on” all the time—one minute I’m buzzing, cracking jokes, feeling like I could train every client at once, and then out of nowhere I get really snappy and pissed off over tiny things, like someone not re-racking weights. My head feels overcrowded. Thoughts come in nonstop—ideas about training, business, my “potential”—and I can’t slow them down or shut them off. Sometimes I catch myself thinking I’m meant to be this kind of legendary trainer, like I’ll revolutionize the fitness world. Lately I’ve also been seeing people in the gym who aren’t actually there—like shadowy figures in the mirrors or someone standing by the squat rack, and when I look again, they’re gone.     D. Schizophrenia

D010-D005_h014.question:

I’ve been “on” almost constantly—barely sleeping, jumping between three or four projects at once, rewriting tools, scanning logs, messaging teammates at 3 a.m. because I feel like I’m seeing patterns no one else is catching. My mind just doesn’t slow down; ideas pile on top of each other so fast I lose track mid-sentence.

My mood swings are all over the place. Sometimes I feel incredible, like I’m invincible and a step ahead of everyone. Then I’ll flip and get irritated over nothing—someone questioning my code, a delayed reply, and I snap or shut down.

And I can’t shake this feeling that my ex is seeing someone else and lying about it—no real proof, but I keep checking her socials, rereading messages, convinced she’s hiding something. It’s starting to mess with my work; I miss details, lose focus, or get stuck chasing these thoughts instead of actual threats.

A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Bipolar II Disorder
    C. Binge-Eating Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia

D010-D005_h015.question:
I guess this all really kicked in about a month ago. It’s like someone flipped a switch. I’ve been feeling weirdly “on top of the world,” almost high without taking anything. I wake up after just a few hours of sleep and I’m buzzing, pacing around my apartment, rearranging gear for jobs that aren’t even booked yet. On scenes I’m moving nonstop—scrubbing, bagging, talking to the cops more than I probably should—like I can’t slow down. My boss told me I’m “too amped” and making people uncomfortable.

My head won’t shut up. Thoughts are flying—one second I’m planning to start my own cleaning company, then I’m thinking about writing a book, then suddenly I’m convinced someone’s tracking me. I keep feeling like there are cameras hidden in the vans, or that the police are watching me specifically, not the scene. I know it sounds off, but it feels real.

And then there are the voices. It’s like a couple of people murmuring about me, sometimes saying I’m being watched, sometimes criticizing how I work. It’s not my own thoughts—they sound separate, like they’re in the room, especially when I’m alone cleaning or trying to fall asleep.

A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Bipolar II Disorder
    C. Binge-Eating Disorder

D010-D005_h016.question:
It’s hard to put everything in order, but I’ll try.

For the last seven months or so, I’ve been really low. I cry at the smallest things—an email from work, a commercial on TV. I used to be very driven in my job, but now I just stare at my laptop and can’t bring myself to deal with even simple HR issues. I’m falling behind on reports, and my team has noticed. Sleep is a mess: I fall asleep, then wake up at two or three in the morning and lie there for hours, going over mistakes I’ve made. Sometimes, when it’s really bad, I’ve thought in detail about ending my life—where I’d do it, how I’d make sure my husband wouldn’t be the one to find me.

Before this long stretch, there was this three‑week period where I felt almost too good. I was buzzing with energy—sending late‑night emails, reorganizing whole departments in my head, starting several new initiatives at once. My mood was sky‑high, like I was on top of everything. My husband said I wouldn’t stop talking, even at home—I’d jump from idea to idea and get irritated if he tried to slow me down.

Around that time, and a bit outside of it too, I became convinced that a senior executive at our company has special feelings for me. He doesn’t say it outright, but I’m sure there are hidden messages in how he writes to me and looks at me in meetings, even though objectively there’s nothing obvious. I also sometimes feel like something is brushing my skin—like a hand on my arm or bugs crawling on my legs—when nothing is there. I’ll slap at my arm or pull up my pant leg, and there’s nothing, but the sensation feels very real in the moment.  

I’m still working, but not well. Things that used to feel manageable now feel either overwhelmingly heavy or, in those high periods, like I’m invincible—then I crash again. My husband says I haven’t been myself for a long time.
D010-D005_h016.options:
A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
D010-D005_h016.answer: D & C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features & Schizophrenia

D010-D005_h017.question:
It’s hard to put into words. For most of this past year, I’ve felt…blank. Not sad exactly, just like there’s nothing inside. I mostly stay in my room. The ladies here knock to see if I’ll join bingo or meals, but I tell them I’m tired and just go back to bed. I can sleep all afternoon after sleeping all night, and still feel like I could lie down again.

I’ve been like that maybe seven months now. During that time I’ve thought a lot about just ending it. I’ve gone over details in my head—where in this building I could do it, what I’d use, when people are least likely to come in. I haven’t acted on it, but it feels very…planned in my mind.

Before this long stretch, there was a few weeks where I was the opposite. I was suddenly full of energy, talking so fast even the nurses told me to slow down. I couldn’t sit still—pacing the halls, rearranging my room at night. I was convinced I was meant for something important, like I had special healing powers and should be in charge here. Around then, I kept smelling strong perfume or smoke that no one else could smell. It all felt very real to me at the time.
D010-D005_h017.options:
A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
D010-D005_h017.answer: D & C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features & Schizophrenia

D010-D005_h018.question:

On and off, I get this conviction that something terrible is about to wipe everything out, like the world’s about to end. Sometimes I smell this strong, burnt, chemical odor in the kitchen or even at home when nothing’s on the stove, and no one else notices it.

    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder

D010-D005_h019.question:
I’m a guide at the museum, so I’m used to talking a lot, but this was…different. About three weeks in the spring, it felt like someone flipped a switch. I was constantly on edge, snapping at visitors for tiny things, arguing with coworkers over details I’d normally ignore. I couldn’t sit still—I'd pace the galleries before opening, reorganize labels that didn’t need it. My husband said I was talking “like a runaway train,” jumping from one idea to the next so fast he couldn’t follow or get a word in. I barely slept but didn’t feel tired then. Since then, it’s gone the other way and stayed that way for about seven months. I feel weighed down and empty most days. I don’t enjoy the art anymore, which scares me; it all looks flat, pointless. Nights are long—I lie there for hours before I can fall asleep. I catch myself thinking it wouldn’t be so bad if I just didn’t wake up, though I’m not planning anything.

    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder

D010-D005_h020.question:
I’ve been driving the school bus for over 20 years, so I’m used to early mornings and a routine. But for about seven months now, I’ve felt like I’m moving through mud. I wake up at 3 or 4 a.m., stare at the ceiling, and can’t fall back asleep. I don’t enjoy anything anymore—kids waving at me, talking to coworkers, even seeing my grandkids—it all feels flat. I’m just…sad all the time. On the worst days, I catch myself thinking it’d be easier if I just didn’t wake up, though I haven’t made any plans.
